sections.html:
Kokomo is the county seat of Howard County, Indiana, about 60 miles north of Indianapolis and 85 miles south of South Bend. The city covers 36.79 square miles at an elevation of 820 feet.

The early Village of Kokomo sat on the south side of Wildcat Creek, and the Nickel Plate Trail now connects with the Industrial Heritage Trail. Freight rail also runs through the city on the Central Railroad of Indianapolis and the Winamac Southern Railway.

The city's nickname is the City of Firsts, a reference to many claimed technical and food-industry innovations.

sections.h2: What is the history of Kokomo?
sections.html:
Kokomo is named for Ma-Ko-Ko-Mo, a Miami man known as Chief Kokomo, although local tradition offers another account involving a Thorntown Miami whose name was written Co-come-wah in an 1834 treaty. Lots were first sold on October 18, 1844.

Residents voted 62 to 3 on October 1, 1855 to incorporate as a town, and Kokomo became a city government in 1865 when Nelson Purdum was elected the first mayor.

A natural gas well came in on October 6, 1886 and started a gas boom. Diamond Plate Glass began in Kokomo in 1887, and Kokomo Opalescent Glass started making stained glass in 1888. Elwood Haynes test-drove his early automobile on Pumpkinvine Pike on July 4, 1894, and the Haynes-Apperson Automobile Company was founded in 1898.

sections.h2: What do Kokomo housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
Kokomo's median owner-occupied home value is $137,400 for 2020 to 2024 according to the Census Bureau, and 63.0% of housing units are owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $939.

The median value here is lower than in Indianapolis, Hobart or Jeffersonville, so repair costs can be a larger share of what a Kokomo house is worth. That is one reason repair-heavy sales are common.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers in Kokomo?
sections.html:
Automobile manufacturing is still a large share of Kokomo jobs. Stellantis lists 3,583 employees at its Kokomo Transmission Plant, 2,439 at the Indiana Transmission Plants I and II and 1,281 at the Kokomo Casting Plant, and the Kokomo Engine Plant began production in 2022.

Other employers include StarPlus Energy, a Stellantis and Samsung SDI joint venture, along with BorgWarner, GM Components Holdings and Haynes International. Higher education adds to the base: Indiana University Kokomo, Ivy Tech Community College, Purdue Polytechnic Institute Kokomo and an Indiana Wesleyan University campus are all in the city.

When a plant adds shifts or cuts them, local housing demand can follow. Sellers with a house tied to a job change often need a firm closing date.

sections.h2: What weather and storm risks affect Kokomo houses?
sections.html:
Kokomo has a humid continental climate with 44.40 inches of precipitation and 34.1 inches of snow in an average year. The record high is 110 degrees and the record low is minus 26, so roofs, furnaces and air conditioners all work hard.

Two storm events stand out in the record. An F4 tornado on April 11, 1965, part of the Palm Sunday outbreak, killed 25 people in the surrounding area. An EF3 tornado on August 24, 2016 damaged about 1,000 homes.

Flooding is part of the history too. In the 1913 flood, Wildcat Creek overtopped its levee and reached nearly a mile wide. Here is what buyers often ask about a Kokomo house:

  • Roof age and any storm repair history.
  • Basement moisture and sump pump condition.
  • Whether the lot is near Wildcat Creek or a mapped flood zone.
  • Furnace and air conditioner age.

sections.h2: How do Kokomo roads and schools factor in?
sections.html:
U.S. 31 was rerouted to bypass Kokomo to the east, opening on November 27, 2013, and the old route became State Road 931.

The Kokomo City-Line Trolley runs five bus routes, and Miller Transportation provides intercity bus service to Indianapolis and South Bend. The Kokomo-Center Township Consolidated School Corporation serves most neighborhoods inside city limits.

Check a specific address against the district's boundaries before you describe it to a buyer.

sections.h2: What city rules apply to Kokomo property owners?
sections.html:
Kokomo has a housing code in Chapter 152 of its municipal code that sets minimum standards for dwellings. Sections cover owners' and occupants' responsibilities, entry for inspections, notices of violation, hearings before a Review Board and enforcement orders.

The code lists maintenance topics including foundations and framing, stairs and porches, gutters and downspouts, plumbing fixtures, water heaters, heating and electrical outlets. It also has a process for unfit dwellings: the code defines an unfit dwelling, allows condemnation and placarding, and requires a condemned building to be vacated.

A separate Rental Housing Officer provision lets the officer inspect structures at reasonable times, and if the owner does not consent, an inspection warrant can be sought. The housing chapter cross-references Chapter 159 for rental housing. If you own a rental, confirm current requirements with the city before you sell.

An open violation or placard can slow a conventional sale, so ask the city whether anything is outstanding on your property.

sections.h2: How does a sale close and get recorded in Howard County?
sections.html:
Kokomo deeds are recorded with the Howard County Recorder in the Howard County Administration Center, 220 North Main Street, Room 330. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and its phone is 765-456-2210.

The recorder keeps permanent public records of transfers between owners, including deeds, mortgages and liens, and its records go back to 1844. Copies of most documents cost $1 per page.

Indiana requires the parties to complete a sales disclosure form, which the county assessor reviews and the auditor files before the deed is filed. Property tax is due in two installments, May 10 and November 10, and the homestead deduction is the lesser of $45,000 or 60% of gross assessed value. Your title company will prorate the taxes at closing.

sections.h2: What do Kokomo sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers in Kokomo tend to meet a handful of repeat situations.

  • An older house with deferred roof, furnace or foundation work.
  • Storm damage that was never fully repaired.
  • A tenant in place or a rental with code questions.
  • An inherited home with several heirs.
  • A job change tied to the area's plants.

Compare offers in writing, and ask each buyer who pays for title and recording.

Before you talk to buyers, it helps to write down what you know about the house. Record the age of the roof, furnace and water heater, any storm or water history, and whether anyone lives in it. A Kokomo house in a city whose median home value is $137,400 may have repair needs that are large compared with its price, and a clear list lets a buyer price those honestly.

If the house was damaged in a storm, gather photos, contractor estimates and insurance paperwork. If it is a rental, gather the lease and rent ledger. If it was inherited, ask the title company or an attorney which documents the county recorder will need before a deed can be prepared.

faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $137,400 for 2020 to 2024, a citywide median that your own house may differ from.

faqs.q: When are Indiana property taxes due?
faqs.a: Indiana property tax is due in two installments, May 10 and November 10. Your closing agent usually prorates the installment.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kokomo house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes, but open violations or a condemnation placard can slow a conventional sale. Ask the city what is outstanding, and compare written cash offers.
